summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was readmitted 48 hours after discharge due to worsening dyspnea, hypoxia, and green secretions. She was found to have hospital-acquired pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, confirmed by sputum culture, and was treated with intravenous antibiotics including meropenem, later transitioned to ertapenem for outpatient completion. She required ICU-level care initially for sepsis with hypotension, which resolved with fluids and pressors. A PICC line was placed to facilitate home antibiotic therapy. Her COPD exacerbation was managed with nebulizers, suctioning, and a short course of prednisone. She stabilized, was weaned to home oxygen, and discharged with home health services and follow-up plans.
